documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

43M, mechanic at an auto repair shop, here to set up primary care. His last PCP closed her practice over the summer and he went months without anyone. Wife made the appointment.

Main issues he brings:
1. Wilson disease. Diagnosed 2017 after his liver tests came back off and he had some slurring of speech and a hand tremor. Sees an outside hepatology group; on trientine 250 mg twice a day and keeps copper low in the diet (no shellfish, nuts, chocolate, liver). Says the speech and tremor settled after treatment started. Gets 24 h urine copper checks through them.
2. Cirrhosis. Hepatology told him his liver is scarred, from the Wilson disease and years of drinking. No known bleeding, no fluid, never been yellow. They follow it.
3. Type 2 diabetes. On metformin 1000 mg twice daily, tolerates it. No home meter readings to share; says his A1c was fine last time.
4. Alcohol. Drank heavily for years; stopped in February of this year on his own and has not had a drink since. Knows he can't go back to it with his liver. Not in a program, says he doesn't need one right now. Open to talking more if that changes.
5. Weight. Has been heavy for a long time.

Tobacco: smoked for years, quit 2016. No vaping. No drugs.
Family: brother has Wilson disease too and got cirrhosis young. Father with type 2 diabetes. Mother with an underactive thyroid.
Allergies: none known.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, trientine 250 mg BID.

ROS: no abdominal swelling, no black stools, no vomiting blood, no confusion, no leg swelling. Energy ok. Works full days on his feet.

Exam: obese man in no distress. No scleral icterus. Mouth and throat normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, nontender, no shifting dullness. No edema. Speech normal, no tremor at rest or with arms out. Skin without spider angiomas.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 0 (abstinent).

A/P
- Wilson disease / cirrhosis, compensated: continue trientine; hepatology owns this, will request their notes. CMP, CBC today.
- T2DM: A1c, UACR, lipids today. Continue metformin. Eye exam this year.
- AUD in remission: congratulated him; door open.
- Prevention: HCV, HIV once. Check hep B immunity given cirrhosis. Flu shot and pneumococcal vaccine next visit with nurse.
- Return 3 months, sooner by text if needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP

Hi Adam, your labs are back. Your diabetes number (A1c) is in a good range. Your liver tests are a little above normal, which fits with what hepatology already knows, and your platelet count is on the low side of normal, also typical with a scarred liver. Kidneys look fine, no protein in the urine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative.

One thing: you are not immune to hepatitis B. With your liver, I'd like you protected. It's a two-shot series a month apart. Can we start it with your flu shot? The front desk will set up a nurse visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, weak, knees ache

HPI: 45M with Wilson disease, compensated cirrhosis and T2DM, came fasting. Over roughly the past year he's been running down: more tired by midafternoon, feels weaker lifting at work. Slow, steady, not sudden. New in the last few months: trouble with erections. Knees bother him a little, worst first thing in the morning and loosening as he moves. Mouth feels dry, sometimes enough that eating is a chore. He mentions, almost as an aside, that people at the shop keep asking where he got his tan. He works inside under the lift, hasn't been in the sun, uses no self-tanner, no new medicines or supplements.

Still no alcohol since Feb 2020. Trientine was raised to 500 BID by hepatology in August.

Family: when asked about iron, says an uncle on his father's side was treated for hemochromatosis. Brother has Wilson disease and got cirrhosis young. Father T2DM, mother hypothyroid.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, trientine 500 BID. NKDA.

Exam: obese, comfortable. Skin with a bronze-gray cast over face, both arms and upper chest, clearly darker than his covered skin. No icterus. Oral mucosa a bit dry, no lesions. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen: liver edge palpable just below the right costal margin, smooth, mildly enlarged, nontender; no ascites, no splenomegaly felt. Hands: second and third MCP joints tender with reduced flexion; other joints of the hands fine. Knees without effusion, full range. No edema.

A/P
1. Fatigue, bronzing, MCP arthropathy, erectile difficulty, hepatomegaly, worsening glucose: picture of iron overload on top of his known liver disease. Iron studies with ferritin and HFE genotype today, along with CMP, CBC, A1c.
2. T2DM: A1c today; same metformin for now.
3. Wilson/cirrhosis: per hepatology; will send them today's results.
4. Vaccines today: flu, bivalent COVID booster, PCV20. Colorectal screening due at 45: FIT kit given.
5. Will call him with the iron and gene results.

conditions.label: Hereditary hemochromatosis with arthropathy
conditions.note: HFE C282Y homozygous; ferritin 1,850, transferrin saturation 78%; MCP arthropathy

documents.title: Results call - hemochromatosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Transferrin saturation 78%, ferritin 1,850. HFE: homozygous C282Y. This is hereditary hemochromatosis, which explains the skin color, the MCP joints, likely the fatigue and erections, and adds iron to an already damaged liver and to the diabetes.

Explained treatment is regular blood removal (phlebotomy) to bring iron down, then maintenance for life. Referring to hematology; their infusion center does the draws. Avoid iron supplements and vitamin C pills, no raw shellfish. His brother and other blood relatives should be checked; he'll tell his brother.

Will send results to hepatology. He asked if this changes the trientine: that's for hepatology to say, I'll flag it in the letter. He verbalized understanding.

documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in 2 years per our routine for him. Letter to pt.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY - NEW CONSULT (brief)
Re: Adam Coughlin, DOB 2/21/1977
Visit 11/07/2022

Referred for HFE C282Y homozygous hemochromatosis with ferritin 1,850 and transferrin saturation 78%. Background of Wilson disease on trientine, cirrhosis followed by hepatology, type 2 diabetes. MCP arthropathy and skin bronzing.
Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: therapeutic phlebotomy, 500 mL weekly as tolerated, Hgb checked before each draw (hold if under 12). Ferritin every 4-6 weeks. Target ferritin 50-100, then maintenance draws spaced to keep it there. First draw done today, tolerated.

Thank you for the referral.
Hematology

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation and Biopsy Result
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY
Patient: Adam Coughlin   DOB: 02/21/1977
Seen 01/09/2023; kidney biopsy 01/23/2023

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Coughlin, 45, with his wife, for edema and proteinuria. Over the last month his lower legs have swollen steadily, he is more tired, and his urine has been foamy and at times darker. He takes his medicines as prescribed and has started nothing new. Background: Wilson disease (diagnosed 2017 with abnormal liver tests, mild dysarthria and tremor; copper-restricted diet and trientine, dose raised about 5 months ago for rising urinary copper), hereditary hemochromatosis on phlebotomy, cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes. Former smoker; alcohol use disorder, abstinent about 3 years. Mechanic.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 36.8 C, BP 130/78, pulse 78, RR 16. Puffy around the eyes. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin both legs. Heart and lungs normal, no crackles, no JVD. No rash, no joint swelling. Mild hepatomegaly, nontender, no ascites.

Data: creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, albumin 2.2 g/dL. Urinalysis 4+ protein, no red cells, no white cells, no casts. 24-hour urine protein 5.8 g/day.

Biopsy (1/23): immunofluorescence shows fine granular IgG and C3 deposits along the glomerular capillary walls, consistent with membranous nephropathy.

Impression: membranous nephropathy with nephrotic syndrome, preserved filtration.

Plan: lisinopril 10 mg daily for proteinuria and furosemide 40 mg daily for edema, both started at the 1/9 visit. Low-salt diet. Given cirrhosis and his infection risk we are holding off on immunosuppression for now and following proteinuria closely. Please check potassium and creatinine in 2-4 weeks; I will see him again in about 3 months.

Nephrology

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - VISIT SUMMARY
Patient: Adam Coughlin  DOB 02/21/1977  Date of service 11/29/2024
Allergies: NKDA

47M, mechanic, with hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, type 2 diabetes and cirrhosis. Small cut to the left hand at work 3 days ago, rinsed with water, nothing else. For 2 days, pain and redness moving up the left arm with fevers and chills.

Vitals: T 38.5 C, HR 100, BP 135/85.
Exam: healing superficial cut on the left hand without abscess or foreign body; red tender streak about 5 cm long running proximally from it; tender left axilla. Hand tendons and range intact.
Labs: WBC 12.0, neutrophils 75%, lymphocytes 15%, CRP 18 mg/L.
Tetanus: Tdap 2021.

Impression: acute lymphangitis, left upper limb.
Disposition: home on amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily x 10 days. Mark the edge of the redness, return for spreading, worse fever or pus. PCP follow-up in 2-3 days.

documents.body:
ED Friday night for lymphangitis of the L arm after a hand cut at work. Day 5 of amoxicillin-clavulanate. Fever gone since Saturday. Arm less sore.

Exam: afebrile. L hand cut closed, clean. Red streak faded, now well below the pen line the ED drew. Axilla barely tender.

A/P: Lymphangitis improving. Finish all 10 days (last dose 12/9). Gloves at work. Call for any new fever or redness.

allergies.reaction: Avoid: penicillin class after amoxicillin hemolytic anemia

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE (abbreviated)
Adam Coughlin, DOB 02/21/1977. Seen 12/09/2024, observed overnight, discharged 12/10.
Allergies on arrival: NKDA. Updated this visit: AMOXICILLIN (immune hemolytic anemia); PENICILLINS, avoid.

Hemochromatosis patient here 10 days after our visit for left-arm lymphangitis. Took the last amoxicillin-clavulanate tablet this morning; a few hours later became very tired and dizzy and noticed dark urine.

T 37.6 C, BP 135/85, P 100, RR 18. Jaundiced. Spleen tip palpable.
Hgb 7.8. Total bilirubin 3.2, direct 0.5. LDH 450. Haptoglobin <10. Smear: spherocytes. Direct Coombs positive, IgG.

Impression: drug-induced immune hemolytic anemia from amoxicillin.
Course: antibiotic already finished. Observed overnight; Hgb stable on recheck, no transfusion. Discharged.
Plan: no amoxicillin or other penicillins. CBC with PCP this week. Hematology informed.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED 12/9 into 12/10 for immune hemolysis from amoxicillin, the day he finished the lymphangitis course. Urine back to normal color since yesterday. Still tired, a bit dizzy on stairs. No chest pain, no shortness of breath at rest, no black stools. Hematology called him: no phlebotomy until his counts recover.

O: Vitals reviewed. Mild scleral icterus. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge as before. L arm: no redness, cut healed.

A/P
1. Drug-induced hemolytic anemia (amoxicillin): allergy list updated with amoxicillin and all penicillins. CBC and bilirubin today. Expect recovery over weeks now that the drug is gone. Repeat CBC early January.
2. Lymphangitis L arm: resolved.
3. HH: phlebotomy on hold per hematology.

Addendum: Hgb 9.1, up from 7.8. Bilirubin coming down.

documents.body: Hgb 11.6, recovering. Bilirubin back near his usual. Recheck in a month. Copy to hematology.

S: Feels like himself again. Energy back. Phlebotomy restarting this month. Nephrology in February, same meds. No drinking, 5 years last month.

Allergies: amoxicillin (immune hemolysis), penicillins.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, trientine 500 BID, lisinopril 10, furosemide 40.

O: No icterus. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge palpable, no ascites. No edema.

A/P
- Hemolytic anemia from amoxicillin: resolved, Hgb normal in Feb.
- MN: creatinine 1.3, drifting up over the last two years. Sent to nephrology.
- T2DM: A1c.
- HH: ferritin crept up during the pause, as expected; hematology resuming.
- 3-4 months.

documents.body: Hi Adam, A1c is fine. Creatinine is 1.3, a little higher than last year, so I've sent it to your kidney doctor. Ferritin rose a bit during the break from draws, which hematology expected.

ED NOTE - brief
Pt: Adam Coughlin, DOB 02/21/1977. Arrived 06/01/2025 06:30.
Allergies: amoxicillin (hemolytic anemia), penicillins.

48M with hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, cirrhosis, membranous nephropathy and type 2 diabetes; immune hemolysis from amoxicillin last December. Cold last week he thought had cleared. Since yesterday severe throat pain, painful swallowing and a muffled voice; can't get his own saliva down; no diabetes pills since yesterday.

T 38.9 C, HR 110, RR 22.
Anxious, sitting bolt upright and leaning forward. Anterior neck tender. Stridor. Drooling.
Glucose 250.
Lateral soft-tissue neck film: enlarged epiglottis, thumbprint sign.

Impression: acute epiglottitis with airway compromise.
Disposition: admitted to ICU for airway monitoring and IV antibiotics. Hospital course per inpatient team; discharged 06/05/2025.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: In the ICU 6/1 to 6/5 with epiglottitis. Was watched closely, never needed a breathing tube per his account. IV antibiotics, then pills to finish at home, done yesterday; doesn't have the name with him. We only have the ED note so far. Throat back to normal, eating and talking fine. Back on metformin since discharge. Lost some weight while he couldn't eat.

O: Afebrile. Voice normal. Oropharynx normal. Neck soft, nontender, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Acute epiglottitis: resolved. Requested discharge summary.
2. T2DM: glucose was high in the ED off his meds and sick. A1c and BMP today.
3. Hemolysis history: reminded him to carry his allergy list.
4. Back in 2-3 months.

Addendum: A1c higher than spring, likely the time off metformin and the illness. Recheck in December before changing anything.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (abbreviated)
Patient: Adam Coughlin   DOB 02/21/1977
Admitted 07/26/2025 via ED to ICU   Discharged 08/02/2025
Allergies: amoxicillin (hemolytic anemia), penicillin

Reason: 48M with hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, cirrhosis, and recent lymphangitis and epiglottitis, two days of increasing neck pain and swelling that started at a tooth, with difficulty swallowing and speaking.
On arrival: T 38.9 C, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air. Firm, brawny, tender swelling of the upper neck and submandibular region; drooling; tongue displaced back and hard to protrude; muffled voice. WBC 18.0 with 80% neutrophils. Glucose 250.

Diagnosis: Ludwig angina.
Course: ICU for airway watch, IV antibiotics, oral surgery extracted the offending tooth. Swelling receded; moved to the floor, then home.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; oral surgery as scheduled.
Home medications unchanged.

procedures.procedure: Transitional care management, moderate complexity

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Home since Saturday after a week in hospital with Ludwig angina from a bad tooth, which was pulled. Swelling gone, swallowing fine, a little sore where the tooth was. Third serious infection in under a year and he's shaken by it. No fever.

Meds unchanged per summary. Allergies: amoxicillin, penicillins.

O: Afebrile. Extraction site healing, no pus. Floor of mouth soft. Neck without swelling or tenderness. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Down to 97.5 kg.

A/P
1. Ludwig angina: resolved. Oral surgery follow-up as booked. Regular dental care matters with his diabetes and liver; he'll find a dentist.
2. Recurrent serious infections in a man with cirrhosis and diabetes: reviewed glucose control and vaccines (up to date). Flu shot in the fall.
3. CBC, BMP today.
4. Recheck in fall.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: WBC back to normal. Hgb fine. Creatinine 1.35, similar to spring. Next labs in September with flu shot.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 48M. Quiet fall, no infections since the summer. Phlebotomy every 2-3 months again. Saw nephrology in October: they're watching the creatinine, same meds. Hepatology in November, trientine unchanged. Found a dentist, cleaning done. Still sober, nearly 6 years. Weight holding a little under 100 kg.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, trientine 500 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, furosemide 40 daily.
Allergies: amoxicillin (immune hemolytic anemia), penicillins.

O: Vitals reviewed. No icterus. Mouth healthy. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge palpable, nontender, no ascites. No edema. Feet: sensation intact, pulses 2+.

A/P
1. Kidney function: creatinine today 1.55 (resulted 12/18), eGFR mid-50s; with September's value that is two readings under 60 three months apart. CKD stage 3a from his membranous nephropathy. Continue lisinopril; avoid NSAIDs; nephrology has the numbers. Metformin dose okay at this level, will review if eGFR keeps falling.
2. T2DM: A1c today.
3. HH: ferritin today.
4. Wilson disease / cirrhosis: hepatology.
5. Return in about 4 months; front desk to book in spring.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: CMP and UACR from 12/17 faxed to nephrology per PCP.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Adam, results from Wednesday: creatinine 1.55, which together with September puts you in stage 3a kidney disease, as we talked about. Diabetes number and iron level are both in range. Nothing to change before your spring visit. Happy holidays.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - brief
Adam Coughlin, DOB 02/21/1977
Admitted 02/04/2026, discharged 02/09/2026, gastroenterology service
Allergies: amoxicillin (hemolytic anemia), penicillin

Presentation: 48M with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease and cirrhosis, history of membranous nephropathy and prior severe infections including Ludwig angina, with two days of vomiting blood and black stools. No trauma, no NSAID use.

Exam: jaundiced. Several spider angiomas over the chest. Liver enlarged and tender below the right costal margin. Abdomen distended with a fluid wave (ascites).

Labs on admission: Hgb 8.2 g/dL; platelets 110,000/mm3; PT 18 s; INR 1.8; PTT 42 s; albumin 2.9 g/dL; total bilirubin 5.1 mg/dL.

Diagnoses: upper GI bleeding; coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency; cirrhosis with ascites.
Treatment: IV vitamin K for the coagulopathy; GI management of the bleed.
Discharge: stable. Follow up with GI and hepatology; see PCP.
